stem: Use the added ideal TCP contact model R_i p + t_i = c, where R_i maps flange vectors to the base frame, p is the unknown fixed TCP offset in flange coordinates, t_i is the flange origin in base coordinates, and c is the unknown fixed contact point in base coordinates. Four observations repeat exactly the same flange orientation and contact pose. After subtracting observation 1 from the others to eliminate c, what can these equations establish about p?

options.text: They become four independent constraints solely because four samples were collected.
They determine p uniquely if the same measurements are averaged often enough.
They determine p uniquely after the same base-origin shift is applied to all observations.
Their rotation differences vanish, so repetitions do not uniquely determine p.

assumptions: Added ideal model of a rigid tool touching the same stationary point; all quantities are expressed in consistent frames and length units. Observations are exact and contain no measurement noise.

stem: What should a sorting implementation use from the labelled photograph rather than assuming that a destination bin must have the same visible hue as its assigned object class?

options.text: Assign destinations by left-to-right detection order, regardless of class.
Assign each object to whichever bin is nearest to its current pick location, regardless of its detected class.
Assign each destination from its current camera hue, ignoring the printed class-to-bin labels.
